items.name: Lightning Bolt (1/Day)
entries: Danny can cast the {@spell lightning bolt} spell once per day, requiring no spell components and using Constitution as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 13}).

items.name: Fey Ancestry
entries: Griff has advantage on saving throws he makes to avoid or end the {@condition Charmed} condition on himself.

items.name: Bouncer's Grip
entries: Griff has advantage on Strength ({@skill Athletics}) checks to grapple a creature.

item.name: Lightningbolt Guitar
entries: This magic guitar flows with the elemental magic of Danny Breeze's music.

entries.name: Battleaxe
entries: This guitar can be wielded as a battleaxe that grants a {@b +2} bonus to attack and damage rolls made with it.

entries.name: Spellcasting Focus
entries: This guitar can also be used as a spellcasting focus; when it is used in this way, the spell attack bonus and save DC of spells that deal Lightning or Thunder damage increase by 1.
It also has the following additional properties. When one of these properties (Lighting Strike or Lightning-bolt) is used, both properties can't be used again until the next dawn.

entries.name: Lightning Strike
entries: When you hit with a melee weapon attack using the guitar, the target takes an extra {@damage 4d8} Lightning damage, and the target must succeed on a {@dc 13} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition Stunned} until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Lightning-bolt
entries: You can use an action to cast {@spell lightning bolt} without expending a spell slot (spell save {@dc 13}).

data.name: The Battle of the Bands
entries: A level 5 one-shot designed for 3 to 6 adventurers set on attending the concert of a lifetime.
by Bryan Mayle
A group of indie musicians…A missing band… And the concert of a lifetime.

You and your indie band-mates are all flunking school, taking time off, or taking a break from adventuring and worked your way to Sharn and the brand new Platinum Dragon arena to see the sold out opening night for Danny Breeze and the Boys' world tour. But something may be amiss, as when you all arrive Danny's band is nowhere to be found! Can you discover the mystery of Danny and his boys? Will you take their place and perform in the career making concert of a lifetime? And most importantly of all, can you make it into the highly exclusive Club Elvinor?

entries.name: Adventure Summary
entries: {@i Battle of the Bands} is a level 5 one-shot designed for 3 to 6 adventurers. The adventure, while 90s themed, takes place atop the Menthis Plateau, in the city of Sharn in the world of Eberron. However, the specifics of the musical genres used can be changed to fit your own world and setting or that of any other official Wizards of the Coast campaign settings.

entries.name: Running this Adventure
entries: To run this adventure, you need the Dungeons & Dragons 5th Edition core rulebooks: Player's Handbook, Dungeon Master's Guide, Monster Manual and Mordenkainen's Tome of Foes.

Text that appears in a box like this is meant to be read aloud or paraphrased for the players when their characters first arrive at a location or under a specific circumstance, as described in the text.
The Monster Manual contains stat blocks for most of the creatures found in this adventure. All the necessary stat blocks are included there or with this module.

entries.name: Introduction
entries: Danny Breeze and the boys are putting on the show of a lifetime at the Platinum Dragon Arena, and the whole world is buzzing about it. The all Genasi bandmates, Danny Breeze, Zane Blaze, Coel Stone and Gurgitem, have swept the nation over the past two years for their music, looks, and charm. Not all is as it seems, however, as this commercial success has been received with scorn and jealousy by {@area Montgomery Bigmoney|MontgomeryBigmoneyNPCBio|x}, CEO of Bigmoney Conglomerate and Bigmoney Records. So much so, that the very night of the concert Danny and the boys were kidnapped, taken to the other side of the city to Bigmoney labs, and Bigmoney attempted to clone them. This created evil half-monster, half-pop punk, elemental creatures now bent on destroying the show.

However, the party knows none of this. Whatever walk of life they come from, there are two truths about this group of adventurers. First, they are part of a so far unsuccessful band of their own. Second, they all have tickets to Danny Breeze and the Boys. There are a number of activities to get up to before arriving at the venue, such as attempting the rite of passage to get their photo on the wall of the illustrious Club Elvinor and if they can't find a way inside on time, well, there's always Christopher E. Mouse, the run down old place across the street.

Once they get to the venue, the arena's manager, {@area Natalie Dublanc|NatalieDublancNPCBio|x}, friend of the party who got them their tickets, comes to them with a problem. The band is nowhere to be found. The party must choose: will they try to find the band before the concert starts or will they try and perform in their place, the potential of starting a world changing music career, or facing the ultimate humiliation of bombing at the highest stakes performance of their lives?

entries.name: Adventure Hook
entries: You have all been sent tickets to Danny Breeze and the Boys' latest and biggest concert ever, part of the Hurricane Heartthrob tour, by the enigmatic friend of one of the party members, {@area Natalie Dublanc|NatalieDublancNPCBio|x}. The reasons for attending the concert can differ from party to party: all or some of the party members could be big fans of Danny and his Boys, going to the musical event of the decade to attempt some industry networking, or simply attending to gain some sense of ironic satisfaction. The precise reasons for attending depend on the specific party, but the free tickets serve as a good motivator.

entries.name: Player Characters
entries: Before character creation there are two important factors to tell your players. This adventure takes place in Eberron, atop the Menthis Plateau in the city of Sharn, though the events of the adventure are highly inspired by 90s music and concerts, players may want to build characters that fit into tropes of characters set in a 90s style media or that of Eberron. More importantly for character creation, the party are all members of a currently unsuccessful indie band, the details of which should be worked out during character creation. Aspects such as the instrument or role they play in the band, its name, and genre of music are the basics of what should be worked out, but feel free to go into as much depth as you like. Other factors include: who founded the band? Why did you all get into music? Are there any creative differences within the band? These are all optional questions to help you flesh out the band.

While this adventure is focused around music, bands, and concerts, it is important to stress during character creation that playing a bard or a high charisma build is not a requirement. Other classes and ability scores will have relevance and their time to shine, both off and on stage.

entries.name: Adapting this Adventure
entries: While this adventure is set in Eberron, it can also be run as part of your own world, or any of the other official Wizards of the Coast campaign settings outside of Eberron. With names changed and references to technology altered if you prefer, the setting can be changed to fit into most traditional D&D fantasy settings.

A pre-existing party does not need to be a part of a preestablished band, however having at least some level of interest in performing music within the party will make this adventure the most enjoyable it can be.

If the backstory of the party members are not conducive to having a character like {@area Natalie Dublanc|NatalieDublancNPCBio|x} in their backstory, the tickets can instead fall into their hands through a number of other means, such as a mysterious random lottery, or on the persons of someone defeated during their normal adventures. Any reference to Natalie talking to the party because of their existing friendship can instead be changed to her recognising the party as capable adventurers.

data.name: NPC Bios
entries: This chapter contains descriptions of the roles and personalities of the notable NPCs present throughout this adventure.

entries.name: Natalie Dublanc
entries: {@i (She/Her) — Drow.} An enigmatic friend of one or more of the player characters. She is now the venue manager of the Platinum Dragon Arena, where the concert is being held. She is friendly, but acts very professional at work, even around friends, and highly stressed on the night of the big event.

entries.name: Montgomery Bigmoney
entries: {@i (He/Him) — Human.} The evil middle-aged CEO of Bigmoney Conglomerate and owner of Bigmoney Records. A jealous man who plotted a kidnapping and arcane cloning scheme after the incredible rise in popularity of Danny Breeze and the Boys. Despite his evil machinations, he is cowardly and sniveling when confronted.

entries.name: Danny Breeze
entries: {@i (He/Him) — Air Genasi.} Head of the band, guitarist and lead vocalist for Danny Breeze and the Boys. Cool head and a cooler smile, his name is on the band for a reason. Laid back attitude and grateful for his fans.

entries.name: Zane Blaze
entries: {@i (He/Him) — Fire Genasi.} Bassist and vocalist for Danny Breeze and the Boys. A hothead who's not too bright, always egging the others on to do outrageous stunts. Has a cool jacket with flaming snakes on the back.

entries.name: Coel Stone
entries: {@i (He/They) — Earth Genasi.} Drummer for Danny Breeze and the Boys. Down to earth and chill, often considered the most grounded of the group, and the emotional glue that keeps the band together.

entries.name: Gurgitem
entries: {@i (They/He) — Water Genasi.} Keytarist for Danny Breeze and the Boys. The mysterious heartthrob of the group, Gurgitem is a man of few words but that hasn't done anything to limit their popularity.

entries.name: Suzanna (Suze) Beldar
entries: {@i (She/Her) — Hill Dwarf.} Bartender at Club Elvinor. Sarcastic but just here to get her job done. Will get hyped when something exceptional occurs.

entries.name: Griff Grumbo
entries: {@i (He/Him) — Sea Elf.} Bouncer at Club Elvinor. Gruff and no nonsense. Loves Danny Breeze and the Boys (Gurgitem is his favourite) and is sad he doesn't have a ticket to the concert.

entries.name: Griff Grumbo Stats Notes
entries: {@creature Griff Grumbo|BMBotB|Griff} is a {@creature Knight} with the following modifications.

items: Griff has advantage on Strength ({@skill Athletics}) checks to grapple a creature.
Griff has the Fey Ancestry trait. (PHB.23)
Griff has proficiency in the perception skill. Granting him a passive perception of 12.

data.name: Chapter 0: Arriving At the Arena
entries: The party arrives at the Platinum Dragon Arena late afternoon, finding themselves in a bustling crowd. They all seem amped to be here, about to see the concert of a lifetime.

It's late afternoon as you all arrive at the theatre district of Menthis Plateau, the center of entertainment in Sharn, and the Platinum Dragon Arena towers above you all, huge posters of the now most popular band in the world Danny Breeze and the Boys adorn the sides with "Danny Breeze and the Boys: Hurricane Heartthrob World Tour" in bold jagged yellow, and pink lettering. There are huge crowds in the square, almost all of them here to see the show.

To recall information about the band Danny Breeze and the Boys, players can attempt a {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill History}) check to recall the names of the band members and their basic personalities as outlined in {@b {@area NPC Bios|NPCBios|x}}, and that they are currently the most popular band in the world. If a player reaches a {@dc 15} on this check, they also learn that their rise to fame began two years ago when they appeared from obscurity with their first hit single {@i Galeforce Love}. They also learn that this rise to fame has been almost entirely independent, as they turned down deals from all record labels who approached them, including the biggest record label in the world Bigmoney Records.

If you wish to include the Exploring The City chapter, the party arrives one hour before admission into the arena, and proceeds directly into {@b {@area Chapter 1: Exploring The City|Ch1|x}}. If you wish to skip that chapter for a shorter experience, the party instead arrives right as admissions begin and you proceed directly to {@b {@area Chapter 2: Entering the Concert|Ch2|x}}.

entries.name: Optional
entries: This chapter is optional. While it is an intended part of the experience, it is able to be cut from the adventure if you wish to condense the one-shot into a shorter timescale. Skipping this chapter will reduce the length of the adventure by approximately 1-1.5 hours.

As you approach the arena you see the admission inside isn't for another hour. You hear a tiefling couple walking away from the admission booth, the taller one talking excitedly. "Do you think we'll have time to check out Club Elvinor? I mean, we have to go right? I bet Danny was there today, what if we get the same seats they sat on!" . The shorter of the two seems doubtful, "I don't know, aren't the lines to get in always, so long?"

If the players want to recall information about Club Elvinor they can attempt a {@dc 8} Intelligence ({@skill History}) check to reveal that Club Elvinor is one of the most prestigious bars in the world in the music scene, and they discover the common saying in the industry. "Any band worth their salt has their picture up on the back wall of Club Elvinor" .

entries.name: Getting Inside Club Elvinor
entries: Once the party arrives outside Club Elvinor, which is also located in the theatre district of the Menthis Plateau, marked by a large sign, they see a large queue stretching outside the entrance, with what they would guess to be a two hour wait time. The party sees a burly Sea Elf bouncer outside the entrance, and across the street a run down Christopher E Mouse restaurant, almost empty.

The party may attempt to convince the bouncer to let them in. The bouncer {@area Griff Grumbo|GriffGrumboNPCBio|x} (Male Sea Elf, {@creature Griff Grumbo|BMBotB|modified Knight}) cares about keeping his job, but is otherwise notably dissatisfied. A successful {@dc 13} Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) reveals his frustration stems from how many people here are going to see Danny Breeze when he is unable to go himself. When attempting to convince Griff to let them inside, a successful {@dc 25} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}), Charisma ({@skill Deception}) or {@dc 28} Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) will convince Griff to let you pass through.

If a player attempts to bribe Griff they must succeed on a {@dc 10} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) check, if they fail the queue of people waiting to get in are outraged, and due to their pressure no benefits of the bribe occur.

items: If Griff is bribed with gold, the DC of Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) checks to enter the club are reduced to {@b 17}.
If Griff is bribed with a ticket to the concert, no roll is required and you will be let inside Club Elvinor. However this may cause complications when the party attempts to enter the concert.

entries: If the party gives up, and does not attempt to enter Club Elvinor, they may instead wait outside the arena, or get food at Christopher E Mouse, which is a resoundingly boring and embarrassing experience for the party as it is clearly targeted towards children.

entries.name: Inside Club Elvinor

entries: The smell of alcohol and cigarette smoke hits you all like a wave as you enter. Inside Club Elvinor, you see the entire building is packed with musicians and fans, and a bored looking Dwarven bartender serving all sorts of drinks. Behind her you see a truly beautiful sight, rows upon rows of framed photographs of some of the most famous musicians and bands of all time, all taken here at Club Elvinor.

The party can either spend their time at the club roleplaying and talking with other people who are at the club or attempting to get a picture of themselves on the wall. If they choose the former, people throughout the bar will all talk about their excitement for the upcoming concert as well as their musical tastes. In these conversations the club patrons will ask the party if they're in a band, and if they say yes, will encourage them to talk to the barkeep and try to get their picture up on the wall to prove their worth.

If the party decides to approach the Hill Dwarf bartender who introduces herself as {@area Suze|SuzeBeldarNPCBio|x} (Suzanna Beldar, {@creature Commoner}) and if they ask how they can get their own picture on the wall she'll explain that they'll have to compete in a {@b {@area Musical Challenge|MusicalChallenge|x}}.

entries.name: Musical Challenge
entries: If the party agrees to compete, a small stage is cleared as the whole crowd turns to watch. Suze lets each of the players pick an instrument from the back, then takes them to the stage to perform a song.

For a musical performance each player rolls initiative to determine order and the contest comprises three rounds. On each turn a player may make a tool proficiency check with their instrument of choice, when making a tool check with their instrument of choice a player may add double their proficiency bonus to the skill check.

The outcome of each round is determined by a skill challenge, where at least half of the party members must beat a set DC with their tool proficiency checks, or another relevant skill if the DM deems it appropriate.
The DC for this musical challenge is {@b 17} and increases by {@b 2} for each subsequent round, if the party succeeds on the skill challenge that round, the DC instead decreases by {@b 1}.

items: If zero or one rounds are a success, the party failed the musical challenge and the whole club seems annoyed and disappointed.
If two rounds are a success, the party gets a small picture put up in the far corner of the bar.
If all three rounds are a success, the party gets a framed picture put up behind the bar.

entries: At the conclusion of the musical challenge, the party realizes it is almost time to enter the arena, and must hurry back.

data.name: Chapter 2: Entering the Concert
entries: With their VIP tickets in hand, the party are able to quickly get past the queues outside and enter the concert arena, however their attention is quickly grabbed by a half-drow woman who the party will recognise as friend and manager of the venue {@area Natalie Dublanc|NatalieDublancNPCBio|x}. Natalie notices the party as they enter the building, and flags them down to speak with them in private.

While Natalie seems calm if a little terse, a {@dc 14} Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check will reveal that she is quite panicked about something, and trying to do some damage control to save some bad situation she's found herself in.

Natalie leads the party to an unpopulated side alley of the arena in an employees only section, where she explains that something has gone wrong and that nobody can find Danny Breeze and the Boys anywhere.

Walking through the packed foyer, you can all feel the excitement in the air permeating through the entire building. However your attention is drawn away from this contagious energy and finding your seats as you notice a half-drow woman in a business suit you all recognise to be the one who got you these tickets, Natalie Dublanc, locks eyes with you all and starts to head towards you.

Natalie will offer the party two options. As she knows they're competent as adventurers, Natalie will ask them if they would want to try and track down the boys and find what happened to them. She will also offer the option- since she knows the party to be musicians themselves- to perform on stage in their place as a surprise opening band in order to find time for security to locate the band.

items: If the party chooses to perform in the concert, proceed on to {@b {@area Chapter 3A: Performing in their Place|Ch3A|x}}
If the party chooses to attempt to find Danny Breeze and the Boys, proceed on to {@b {@area Chapter 3B: Finding the Boys|Ch3B|x}}

data.name: Chapter 3A: Performing in their Place
entries: If the party chooses to perform in the place of Danny Breeze and the Boys, Natalie will tell them to quickly get any instruments and supplies needed from the backroom and to hurry backstage. Once backstage assistants will rush to provide any makeup and outfits needed.

entries.name: Playing the Opening Number
entries: After these brief preparations the party are all ushered onto the stage to a sea of thousands of fans who were expecting to see Danny Breeze and the Boys. The party must make a {@dc 15} Wisdom saving throw or become {@condition Frightened} before their opening song.

With instruments in hand you all walk out onto stage to the thunderous applause and uncontrollable excitement of the crowd. That is however, until they quickly notice that you are not Danny Breeze and the Boys. That adoration is quickly replaced with confusion and the terrifying gaze of thousands of people attempting to work out just who you are and what's happening, the immense pressure bearing down on you all.
For their first song on stage the party must perform another {@b {@area Musical Challenge|MusicalChallenge|x}} as outlined in Chapter 1, however the starting DC is set to {@b 18}.

items: At the end of each round of the Musical Challenge any {@condition Frightened} character can repeat their saving throw, removing the condition on a success.
If zero or one rounds are a success the party fails the musical challenge, they are booed and heckled by the crowd, who are demanding Danny Breeze and the Boys.
If two rounds are a success the crowd is enthused, but still seem impatient waiting for Danny Breeze and the Boys.
If all three rounds are a success the crowd goes wild, cheering and screaming in support of the party's band, with no mention of Danny Breeze and the Boys.

entries.name: Danny Breeze Arrives
entries: No matter the outcome of this first song, after its conclusion a rift opens in the center of stage and out steps someone who appears to be {@area Danny Breeze|DannyBreezeNPCBio|x}, followed by four figures that look somewhat like his Boys, the rift closing behind them.

Danny's boys immediately look wrong and elemental. {@area Zane Blaze|ZaneBlazeNPCBio|x}'s body shifts and morphs like fire, {@area Coel Stone|CoelStoneNPCBio|x} has a face of unmoving rock and {@area Gurgitem|GurgitemNPCBio|x} is translucent and wobbles as he moves, all with instruments in hand.

While {@creature Danny Breeze|BMBotB|Danny} himself seems normal at first glance, a successful {@dc 13} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check reveals his twisted elemental nature as well, with parts of his body breaking away into wisps of air and wind before reforming in small parts all around his body.
The party can quickly realize that these are not the real Danny Breeze and the Boys, but some kind of fakes.

Danny taunts the party, insulting their performance if they succeeded on two or less rounds of the musical challenge, or berates them for attempting to upstage him at his own concert if they succeeded on all three. Danny then turns to rile up the audience, before attacking the party.
While the clone of Danny Breeze is mostly articulate, the others are less intelligent and mostly repeat cool phrases that stereotype their originals' personalities.

Throughout the fight you should describe the boys losing their humanoid forms, becoming more elemental and primal as they take damage. By the time a bandmate other than Danny is below a quarter of their max hp they should no longer resemble a humanoid at all and be fully elemental. Danny retains his mostly humanoid form until death where he scatters to the wind.

entries.name: Fighting Danny Breeze and the Boys
Stats for Danny Breeze and the Boys
entries: The recommended stat blocks for Danny Breeze and the boys are as follows.

items: {@creature Danny Breeze|BMBotB} is a modified {@creature Air Elemental Myrmidon|MTF} with a Charisma score of 20, a max hp of 100 and can cast the {@spell lightning bolt} spell once per day using his Constitution modifier {@b (Save DC 13)}.
Zane Blaze is a {@creature Fire Elemental} with a Charisma score of 18 and a max hp of 70.
Gurgitem is a {@creature Water Elemental} with a Charisma score of 18 and a max hp of 80.
Coel Stone's is an {@creature Earth Elemental} with a Charisma score of 18 and a hit point maximum of 90.

entries.name: Adjusting The Difficulty
entries: If you want to make this encounter slightly easier, change either Zane Blaze to {@creature Zane Blaze (Mephit)|BMBotB} (a modified {@creature Magma Mephit} with a max hp of 35) or change Coel Stone to {@creature Coel Stone (Mephit)|BMBotB} (a modified {@creature Dust Mephit} with a max hp of 40). If you want to make this encounter much easier, make both of them mephits.

items: Two mephits will be an easy encounter for a party of 3-4 players, while one mephit will be an easy encounter for a party of 5-6 players. Having one mephit is recommended for a party of 3-4 players.
For each band member that is replaced by a mephit, describe their diminished form and frailty in comparison to the others.

entries.name: The Stage
entries: The Stage is 100 feet across and 40 feet deep. The party begins combat in the middle, with Danny Breeze and the boys 30 feet to one side. The drop from the stage to the ground is 5 feet.

entries.name: Winning Over the crowd
entries: An important element to this combat is the audience, who as an Environmental Action on Initiative 0 (losing ties) can provide various effects to either the party or Danny Breeze and the Boys.

At the end of every player character's turn, the character that ended their turn makes a {@dc 15} ability check in order to sway the crowd. The skill used in this ability check is either a Charisma ({@skill Performance}) check or a Performance check with the ability score determined by the primary ability score used by the creature during that turn. For example a wizard who cast {@spell chromatic orb} on their turn could make an Intelligence ({@skill Performance}) check to win over the crowd, or a Barbarian who took the Attack action could make a Strength ({@skill Performance}) check.

Keep track of the number of successes from the party. If half or more of the players succeeded that round they temporarily sway over the audience; if not, the audience is swayed by Danny Breeze and the Boys. At Initiative 0 (losing ties) the audience takes an environmental action to cause one of the following effects to aid either the party or Danny Breeze; the audience can't use the same effect two rounds in a row:

items: The audience cheers inspire strength. Each member of the band that swayed the audience each gains {@dice 2d6} temporary hit points.
The audience throws healing potions from the crowd splashing against the most injured party member. The most injured member of the band that swayed the audience regains {@dice 2d4 + 2} hit points.

The audience jeers and boos the other team, each member of the band that did not sway the audience must all make {@dc 14} Wisdom saving throws or have disadvantage on the first attack, ability check or saving throw they make before the end of the next round.
The audience begins chanting the name of the band that swayed them. Each member of this band has advantage on the next attack roll or saving throw they make before the end of the next round.

entries.name: Beating Danny Breeze and the Boys
entries: Once Danny Breeze and the Boys are defeated the crowd goes wild, cheering and shouting the name of the party's band. Where the bodies of the Elemental would be, the party instead finds glowing crystals with the letters B.M. engraved on them and Danny Breeze's {@item Lightningbolt Guitar|BMBotB}. A successful {@dc 12} Intelligence ({@skill History}) check reveals this to be the logo of the Bigmoney Conglomerate.

Upon picking up one of the crystals, the rift Danny Breeze and the Boys entered through reopens, where the party can see the inside of a laboratory with the same B.M. logo. Inside the room the party can see the real Danny Breeze and the Boys tied up and gagged by the far wall.
When the party enters the rift proceed to {@b {@area Chapter 4: Confronting Bigmoney|Ch4|x}}.

data.name: Chapter 3B: Finding the Boys
entries: If the party decides to track down Danny Breeze and the boys, {@area Natalie|NatalieDublancNPCBio|x} swiftly leads them to the green room where they were last seen, talking nervously the whole way.

entries.name: Searching the Green Room
entries: The green room is messy with no immediate sign of violence having taken place. If a character succeeds on a {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) or Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check, they find that the lock on the window to the green room was broken. If a character instead succeeds on a {@dc 13} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) or Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) on this check, they further discover faint scorch marks around the window frame, which they can intuit as being a product of Zane Blaze being moved through the window unconsciously. They also learn that the window was broken from the outside.

A {@dc 15} on this check reveals a cracked lanyard knocked behind one of the couches, presumably torn off in some sort of struggle, it is a simple lanyard with a runestone with the insignia B.M. Labs on it. A successful {@dc 12} Intelligence ({@skill History}) check reveals this to be Bigmoney Labs, which is an hour away from the stadium on the Central Plateau. If none of the players succeed on this check, Natalie will provide the information instead.

entries.name: Entering the Lab
entries: The party can quickly make their way across Sharn and up to the Central Plateau to Bigmoney Labs without much trouble—however it starts raining and storming as they get close. The lab is a large gray building with three security guards outside, and a large glass door with a runestone reader at the front, as well as a side entrance.

The party can sneak past the guards if at least half of the party make a successful {@dc 12} Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) check to get to the side door, or a {@dc 15} Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) check to get to the main entrance. The guards can also be persuaded to leave if bribed with gold with a {@dc 18} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) check, or convinced to leave with a {@dc 18} Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) check.

You make haste across the city, towards Bigmoney Labs atop the Central Plateau, making good pace as you move from street to street, dodging vehicles and pedestrians alike. Eventually you find yourselves cloaked by the shadows of an imposing tower blotting out the sun, with the name "Bigmoney Labs" placed proudly on the front. When you set your eyes on the oppressive structure, the skies open up with wins and rain as lightning illuminates the sky.
The security guards consist of one guard captain ({@creature Knight}) and two guards ({@creature Guard}). If the captain dies or is knocked unconscious the guards will flee.

The runestone the party collected can be used to unlock both the main door and the side door. The doors can also be opened with a {@dc 13} tool proficiency check (Thieves' Tools) or a {@dc 15} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check.

Once the party enters the lab they can hear the sounds of glass shattering in the central room ahead, and when they enter the room they see four broken glass containers suspended in the air above four large vats each one which a different color and element, once containing the failed clones of Danny Breeze and the Boys who have now broken free.

In the room beyond the party sees the middle aged businessman {@area Montgomery Bigmoney|MontgomeryBigmoneyNPCBio|x}, along with the tied up original members of Danny Breeze and the Boys. Bigmoney, upon seeing the party, presses a button to close metal security shutters to the innermost room he and the original boys are in, blocking access.

As you all rush into the laboratory, you see four large shattered glass containers, each suspended above a vat of acidic liquid each of a different color. On the ground in front of each of them are creatures that look somewhat like Danny Breeze and the Boys but clearly something else. Larger and less humanoid, swirling in raw elemental energy they all snap their heads to look at you with burning eyes, instruments in hand. Behind them you see a window into a room beyond, where you see a large, middle-aged man some of you would recognise as Montgomery Bigmoney, as well as four tied up bodies you instantly know to be the real Danny Breeze and the Boys. Before you can act Montgomery, watching you all, presses a button closing heavy metal shutters around the windows and door to that innermost lab.

The clones of Danny Breeze and the Boys are clearly unstable, looking more like full elementals than genasi, with Danny looking the most humanoid of them all. Driven to a violent frenzy the elemental band attacks the party.

entries.name: Fighting Danny Breeze and the Boys
entries: While the clone of Danny Breeze is mostly articulate, the others are less intelligent and mostly repeat cool phrases that stereotype their originals' personalities.
Chapter 3A has {@b {@area Stats for Danny Breeze and the Boys|DannyBreezeAndBoysStats|x}}, including tips for adjusting the difficulty.

entries.name: Acid Vats
entries: There are four vats of acid in the lab each corresponding to a different damage type and band member:

Any creature that falls into one of these vats must make a {@dc 13} Constitution saving throw or take {@damage 4d8} damage of the vats respective type, taking half as much on a successful save. A creature must make this save the first time it enters the vat on a turn or ends its turn there. Each member of Danny Breeze and the Boys is immune to the damage of their respective vat, and vulnerable to the damage from the others.
Climbing out of a vat requires a {@dc 10} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) or Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check as part of a creature's movement. It can repeat this check with its action.

entries.name: End of the fight
entries: Once Danny Breeze and the boys are defeated the security shutters to the back room with Bigmoney are opened and the party can head through the main door to the innermost laboratory.

data.name: Chapter 4: Confronting Bigmoney
entries: Once Danny Breeze and the Boys have been defeated, {@area Montgomery Bigmoney|MontgomeryBigmoneyNPCBio|x} does not put up much of a fight.
The party enters the innermost laboratory either through a rift from the stage in {@area Chapter 3A|Ch3A|x} or the main door from {@area Chapter 3B|Ch3B|x}.

In the back of the room the original Danny Breeze and the Boys are tied up and semi-conscious. As the party approaches, Montgomery Bigmoney ({@creature Commoner}) emerges from behind a corner. He's a large, sweaty human man in a business suit.

Bigmoney will go on to explain his plan. How Danny Breeze and the Boys turned the offer for a record deal at Bigmoney Records and were too hot headed to work with him, so he planned to kidnap the band, and clone them with the clones performing in their place and signing on for a record deal. The clones didn't work out perfectly however, and broke out of their pods malformed and incomplete, too violent to be useful.
The party can dispose of Bigmoney however they feel fit before, during, or after this explanation.

data.name: Chapter 5: Ending the Adventure
entries: Once they free Danny Breeze and the Boys, the now weakened band will be incredibly grateful and will ask the party if they want to do the rest of their tour together. Grateful for their rescue, Danny Breeze gifts the party his {@item Lightningbolt Guitar|BMBotB}. If the party accepts they head back to the arena with the real Danny Breeze and the boys playing a song together that will rocket them into stardom.

The adventure ends during this first song they sing alongside Danny Breeze and the Boys. If you wish to continue this adventure in future sessions, try to think of the new issues and enemies that this sudden rise to stardom may cause for your party.
